lens: ChatGPT / OpenAI-native: conversation-first, minimal, Realtime voice-mode aesthetic that showcases OpenAI models
name: Orb-First Coach Console
one_liner: Voice-mode minimalism for the live call, with a dense coach rail beside it: one orb, one transcript, one shadcn/ui system, and OpenAI model state always visible. Self-scores: A 8, B 8, C 8, D 6.5, E 6.5, F1 6 (crowded field), F2 6.5 (self-hosted licences), F3 3 (10 = not worth building).
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: conversation-first, minimal, Realtime voice-mode feel (dark orb stage, warm light UI, one primary action per screen). Changed: research showed coaching is the gap. Second Nature's Deal Coach coaches live deals, not practice calls, and Yoodli coaches on real calls (secondnature.ai, yoodli.ai). Hyperbound scores real calls against practice scorecards (mindtickle.com). Mobbin voice screens (ElevenLabs, Grok, Hume) are single-pane chat with no live scoring, so I added a persistent coach rail and a live rubric. Current voice runs on ElevenLabs only, so OpenAI Realtime must be added as a first-class engine.

ui_stack.name: shadcn Command (cmdk) and Drawer (vaul)

palette.use: Cards, sheets and the coach rail
Dark voice stage on the call screen and landing hero
Live state, orb, positive bars; graphics and dark surfaces only
Anything produced or graded by a model: cues, wizard draft, grader chip
Objection and missed-criterion bars; use alert-text #C2410C for text on light

design_language.typography: Geist 600 for display (48/52 landing, 28/34 page titles). Geist 400 at 15/22 for body. Geist Mono 13/18 with tabular numerals for timers, scores and model IDs. Sentence case throughout; all-caps only on 11px state tags.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 16px radius on cards and sheets, 28px on the composer, pill chips. 1px hairlines carry structure. One soft shadow, reserved for floating cue cards. The orb is the only glow in the product.
design_language.motion: 180ms ease-out for state changes. The orb tracks live audio level while idle and while speaking. Cue cards slide in from the rail edge. Debrief scores count up once. Under prefers-reduced-motion everything becomes a fade.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 20px with 1.5px stroke. Mic, waveform and clock glyphs signal voice state. No emoji in product UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default on the call screen and landing hero for the voice-mode feel. Light is the default for library, wizard, debrief, progress and team. Both sets share token names: dark canvas #0B0C0E, surface #15171B, line #2A2D33, ink #F4F4F2. Follows system preference with a user override.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a 64px icon rail that expands to labels with Practice, Library, Progress and Team (Team shows only inside an org). The top bar holds a Cmd+K persona search and a model-status chip (Voice, Coach, Grader, with a Heuristic fallback state). Routes: / landing; /library with facets; /library/new wizard; /practice/[id] briefing; /call/[id] live; /debrief/[id]; /progress; /team. Mobile: a bottom tab bar with four items and a centre Create button. The scenario editor folds into a persona drawer instead of a separate long form page. Login, MFA and access-code pages keep their current flows, restyled.

screens.layout: Full-bleed 390px. The top 40% is the dark stage: orb centred, state label beneath, and the current line only as a caption; swipe up opens the transcript sheet. live_coaching_and_scoring: Two channels. The persona voice model (Realtime, or the existing ElevenLabs agent) stays in character and never coaches. A separate coach call runs after each rep turn with the rubric, talk track and last six turns, and returns structured cue and criterion-state data with transcript line references. Cues should appear within about two seconds of the rep finishing a turn. The rail labels scores live estimate until final grading, which stays authoritative. Cue types: objection alert, next-best question, talk-track step, pricing or compliance flag. Each cue carries its evidence quote, Accept or Dismiss, and a feedback button. Coaching intensity (Quiet, Cues, Full) controls volume, and Quiet still scores. When the grader falls back to heuristics, the chip says so.
persona_library_and_wizard: Launch target: about 150 personas in 15 job families (SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections), each with four to six objections and a rubric template. Each persona is one Markdown file with front matter, so a contributor adds one by PR and the library renders it without a code change. Filters: role, industry, difficulty, objection type, mode. The wizard accepts a job description, product URL, CRM note, ICP or pasted call, asks one question at a time, streams a draft card, runs a 60-second test call, and saves locally or exports a PR-ready file. Self-score E 6.5, because content volume is the real risk.
signature_moments: The coach rail whispers a cue on the exact turn the rep needs it, with the quote that triggered it.
The orb is driven by real audio levels, so the stage visibly listens and speaks.
Model chips on every surface (voice, coach, grader, wizard), with per-call cost in mono.
Replay from this moment: one missed turn in the debrief becomes the next practice call.
A dark voice stage that becomes a light scorecard, all from one token set.
openai_fund_angle: The model showcase sits in the chrome, not a footer. A model-status chip on the call, debrief and dashboard names the voice engine (OpenAI Realtime added beside ElevenLabs), the coach model and the grader model, plus per-call tokens and cost. Attribution reads Built on OpenAI as plain text with no logo, to respect trademark rules. For contributors: a Contribute page lists good-first-issue personas, each with a draft-with-Codex link and a how-to. An AGENTS.md at the repo root explains the persona format and tests. Persona cards show author handles and open PRs. Codex-run persona lint and rubric-weight checks in CI support the Codex for Open Source story (PR review and maintainer automation).

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0: palette tokens, Geist, shadcn init, and wrappers around the existing .card, .btn-primary and .input classes. Phase 1: shell, landing, library and persona files. Phase 2: briefing, live call with coach rail behind a flag, and debrief. Phase 3: wizard, progress and team. Phase 4: mobile pass, WCAG AA contrast audit and reduced-motion check. Keep Tailwind 3 until phase 4, then evaluate v4. Persona content and the coach channel are separate work items that need their own owners.

risks: Coach latency: a second model call per turn can exceed two seconds. Fall back to end-of-turn cues and say so in the UI.
Trust: live estimates that differ from the final grade will confuse reps. Label them clearly and keep the final grade authoritative.
Content volume: 150 personas is a large writing task. Ship about 40 at launch and mark the rest as roadmap.
Cost: per-call voice spend may deter open-source users. Show cost, and keep text mode as the free default.
Trademark: OpenAI attribution must not imply endorsement. No logo, and no OpenAI-specific colours beyond the custom palette.
Mobile patterns come from web Mobbin results; no iOS search was run. Mobbin imagery is for internal inspiration only and must not ship.

Mobbin notice, verbatim (tooling, not a product risk): **Your Mobbin AI usage is high this month** Usage is unlimited during beta. If your usage stays at this level, you may need to purchase more credits once limits take effect. [View usage and plan options](https://mobbin.com/settings/billing-and-usage)
